The Road To Loch Nam Bairneas

Beautiful tune composed by Allan MacDonald.
Transcribed off Beòlach’s album, *All Hands*.

↳ Posted by bdh on February 25th, 2020.

Re: The Road To Loch Nam Bairneas

Quite popular recently.
Ross Couper and Tom Oakes play it in F#m. I also heard Adam Sutherland and Emma Tomlinson play it at last year’s Fèis Rois nan Inbheach (it was either in Em or Am - can’t quite remember). So a very malleable tune.
I’ll maybe post Ross Couper’s take.

↳ Posted by DonaldK on February 25th, 2020.

The Road To Loch Nam Bairneas, X:2

This is roughly how Ross Couper and Tom Oakes play Loch nam Bairneas, in F#m (not A).

Not a reel, of course. Allan MacDonald calls it a quickstep. It’s in both The Nineties Collection and The Moidart Collection II. In the former it’s pointed but in the latter (and later volume) it’s straight.

↳ Posted by DonaldK on February 25th, 2020.

Re: The Road To Loch Nam Bairneas

I’m learning to play this pipe tune with a piper and others. The setting X:1 is in the right key and correct, but the fourth part differs the second time around needing 16 bars to notate it or else a primo/secondo 1/2 repeat section.
Version : X:2 seems to be right in part 4, but is not in the right key.

↳ Posted by Philip W on October 12th, 2022.

The Road To Loch Nam Bairneas, X:3

See my comment above. I taken the last eight bars of X:2, transposed them to the original piper’s key, and added them to X:1. Thus bars 3 and 4 of the repeated eight are now changed as bars 11 and 12 of the 16 bar final part.
I am finding these two bars the hardest to learn. Great tune, though.
Now I can practise playing along with the improved play audio feature which allows me to adjust the playback speed.
I found that version X:2 is not only 4 semitones lower in pitch but does vary from the original more than I first thought.

↳ Posted by Philip W on October 22nd, 2022.

Re: The Road To Loch Nam Bairneas

The Couper/Oakes setting in F#m is 5 semitones down, Philip.
The first setting misses the fourth part variation because it is taken from the Béolach recording (and they miss the variation, as well as playing a few other bits differently to Allan’s original).

The Road To Loch Nam Bairneas -finally matching how the composer plays

Sorted! Now the setting matches what the composer plays on his website. Except for the pipers’ grace notes.
Allan MacDonald is remarkable for what he has achieved. Go to his website;
https://allanmacdonald.com/.
To hear him playing this tune go to
https://allanmacdonald.com/music/
and it’s six tunes up from the bottom of a list of about thirty sound files.

The Road To Loch Nam Bearneas

A 2/4 pipe march, or “quickstep” by Allan MacDonald, as published in “The Nineties Collection”.
Another version of this tune is filed under “reels”: https://thesession.org/tunes/19038

↳ Posted by Malcolm Reavell on October 28th, 2024.

Re: The Road To Loch Nam Bairneas

In The Nineties Collection it’s spelled “Bearneas”. In Allan MacDonald’s second collection (Moidart Collection II) it’s consistently spelled “Bairneas”. On OS maps it’s called “Loch na Bairness”, southwest of “Cruach na Bairness”.

Note that in Allan’s second collection, published after The Nineties Collection, the tune is presented straight rather than pointed.

If you want it reclassified as a March, Malcolm, you can do that through the EDIT THIS TUNE tab at the top right of the page.

↳ Posted by DonaldK on October 28th, 2024.

The original link is thesession.org/tunes/19038
